content:
Twenty of the fifty questions on an SOF IMO paper are not school maths at all — they are reasoning. Series, coding, directions, ranking. No textbook chapter covers them, which is exactly why practised students gain a full section on the field. Take the free IMO Class 8 Logical Reasoning online test below before any revision. Ten MCQs, instant score, full explanations — it will tell you exactly what to fix first.

What the IMO asks from Logical Reasoning in Class 8

  • Number and letter series; alphabet position work.
  • Coding–decoding with shifts and patterns.
  • Direction sense and distance after a walk.
  • Ranking and ordering; simple Venn logic.
  • Mirror images, water images and embedded figures.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Anchor letters with EJOTY: E = 5, J = 10, O = 15, T = 20, Y = 25 — positions come instantly.
  • The opposite of any letter sits at 27 minus its position: C (3) pairs with X (24).
  • Mirror images swap left–right; water images flip top–bottom. Different questions, different flips.
  • When a series misbehaves, take differences OF the differences — second layers hide there.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Tracking turns mentally in direction puzzles instead of sketching the path.
  • Using rank-from-left + rank-from-right without subtracting the double-counted person.
  • Forcing one constant difference onto a series that alternates two rules.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ___
questions.explanation: The differences between consecutive terms are 4, 6, 8, 10. These differences increase by 2 each time, so the next difference is 12. Therefore, the next term = 30 + 12 = 42.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 1, 4, 13, 40, 121, ___
questions.explanation: Each term is obtained by multiplying the previous term by 3 and adding 1. So: 1 × 3 + 1 = 4, 4 × 3 + 1 = 13, 13 × 3 + 1 = 40, 40 × 3 + 1 = 121, 121 × 3 + 1 = 364.

questions.q: Find the next letter in the series: A, C, F, J, O, ___
questions.explanation: The positions of the letters are 1, 3, 6, 10, 15. The gaps between positions are +2, +3, +4, +5, which increase by 1 each time. The next gap is +6, so the next position = 15 + 6 = 21, which is the letter U.

questions.q: If '+' means 'x', '-' means '+', and 'x' means '-', then what is the value of 6 + 3 - 8 × 2?
questions.explanation: Replace the symbols according to the given code: 6 × 3 + 8 - 2. Applying BODMAS: 6 × 3 = 18, then 18 + 8 - 2 = 24.

questions.q: In a certain code, TIGER is written as UJHFS. How is MOUSE written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted forward by 1 position in the alphabet: T+1=U, I+1=J, G+1=H, E+1=F, R+1=S. Applying the same rule to MOUSE: M+1=N, O+1=P, U+1=V, S+1=T, E+1=F. The code is NPVTF.

questions.q: In a survey of 100 people, 60 like tea, 45 like coffee, and 20 like both tea and coffee. How many people like only tea?
questions.explanation: People who like only tea = Total who like tea - Those who like both = 60 - 20 = 40.

questions.q: In a class of 60 students, 35 passed in Mathematics and 30 passed in Science. If 10 students passed in both subjects, how many students failed in both?
questions.explanation: Students who passed at least one subject = 35 + 30 - 10 = 55. Students who failed both = 60 - 55 = 5.

questions.q: Introducing a man, a woman said, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.explanation: The only daughter of the woman's mother is the woman herself. So the man's mother is the woman. The woman is the man's mother.

questions.q: Aman walks 12 m North, then turns left and walks 5 m, then turns left and walks 12 m. How far is he from the starting point and in which direction?
questions.explanation: Starting at (0,0). Walk 12 m North: (0,12). Turn left (face West), walk 5 m: (-5,12). Turn left (face South), walk 12 m: (-5,0). He is at (-5,0), which is 5 m West of the starting point.
